Params: Allow me to tell you a story.
A story of a girl who once believed she could save the world—only to be betrayed by it in the end.
Having been saved once herself, longing to return the kindness she received, the girl made a wish to an Angel—so that she too might become someone who could bring smiles to others.
She fought with everything she had, determined to prove herself to the woman who guided her on the path to becoming an Angel, and to repay that kindness.
She would smile and look at the girl with approval.
And so the girl fought harder still, pushing herself to the point of burning out.
[May my efforts be rewarded. May my strength truly help someone.]
The girl held such a conviction, never once faltering. No, in fact, she only burned brighter, reducing everything before her to ash—
Then, that fateful day came. She pushed through the smoke as she always did after the battle ended, only to find her dearest friend lying still on the ground.
But even in her final moments, there was no pain on her face. There was only that familiar smile, as if they were simply parting ways after class.
Though no words could reach her now, she knew with absolute certainty that her friend would offer such gentle comfort, even to the one who killed her.
Her eyes snapped open from the nightmare, only to find herself in an even more unfamiliar place.
A strange, sweet fragrance filled the air, and everyone around her seemed lost in some inexplicable fervor.

She couldn't help but feel on edge in the face of such an eerie scene, and instinctively reached for her waist with her right hand. Her flintlock pistol, imbued with Zafkiel's power, should've been there.
But all her fingers found was an intricately crafted pocket watch with a vintage design.
...Something isn't quite right here. It's almost as if... this place has weakened Zafkiel's powers.
She tried to retrace her steps, to recall how she ended up here—but the harder she pushed herself to remember, the pain stabbing through her mind only grew sharper.
In the end, she had no choice but to set the agonizing attempts aside and turn her attention to the surroundings instead.
There's no need to push yourself. Just rest for now.
A tall figure clad in black crouched down beside her, offering a steaming cup of something warm.
You must have just arrived in this "Dream City."
Please rest assured. I'll be right here with you and help you "find a way back."
In order to find a way back to reality and uncover how she ended up here in the first place, the girl began traveling alongside this human named 【kuroname】.
That person has always spoken of things that sound like utter nonsense to her, like coming from a world destroyed by something called the Punishing Virus.
That world is nothing like this place. It is cruel, desolate, and is all but overflowing with despair.
And yet, despite it all, that person remains determined to give up everything here and return to that world which seemingly has nothing left to offer.
You can see it too, can't you? Even if this is all just a dream...
Compared to that world, there's at least some hope left in this place.
Because there are people waiting for me to go back.
The human who always walked ahead, clearing the obstacles in her path, stopped in their tracks.
To me, every single soul matters. I'm going to find a way for everyone here to escape this dream...
And I'll find a way to create new hope, for the people of that world as well.
The girl fell silent. That's because she was beginning to understand, though only a little, the reason she had ended up here.
Still, she was afraid to face the truth.
And so, the first ending befell them. The human, too, held fast to that conviction until the very end.
Such a shame... I went to all that trouble crafting the perfect dream for you, and yet you refuse to savor it until the very end.

The being known as The Oneiros tore open the "door" with her own hands, unleashing a torrent of nightmares from the deepest recesses of the dream. In an instant, the pristine paradise became a sea of blood.
You could have enjoyed yourselves to your hearts' content, then become nourishment for this dream without ever knowing anything...
But since you've chosen to defy me, this paradise has no further use for you.

Hundreds upon hundreds of nightmares surged forward like a roaring tide, entangling the human and the girl. Despite their desperate struggles, they're pushed back step by step under the relentless onslaught.
Amid the surging black tide, you stepped forward, placing yourself squarely between Kurumi and the nightmares.
Even as claws tore into your arm, even as blood began streaming down, you refused to budge an inch.
In the middle of the murky sea, the girl and the human stood back to back. Her fierce voice rose, questioning the figure looming above.
All you've done is trap all these people here, feed them sweet lies laced with poison. Do you really think that's enough to build your precious paradise?!
Haha... Now isn't that ironic, coming from you, Miss Tokisaki.
The tall woman hovers above the sea of mud, her lips curling into a wicked smile as she gazes down at the two with utter disdain.
You know better than anyone why you chose to come here, don't you?
The words pierce through her mind like a spike, and the pain erupts. Countless images flash wildly before her eyes—
Shattered crystals, a resolute figure, the touch of something cold, and whispers both blurred and tender... Her vision flickers, threatening to drag her away into the deluge of memories.
Don't apologize to me, okay? Otherwise, we'll just end up saying sorry to each other forever.
You know, now that I think about it... Being with you made me really happy...
In that moment, Kurumi Tokisaki finally understood—her own memories were sealed within the pocket watch this whole time.

The moment she fell into this "dream," she cast aside everything tied to Zafkiel. She tossed away all the anguish along with the power that had once been her salvation, burying it all into the deepest corners of her heart.
What a laughably naive and childish dream.
A world where you were never deceived, where you never made a single mistake?
What a dull wish. I see no desire in it, nor a single trace of ambition to change anything.
Even though you only became the Spirit of Time by exploiting the sacrifices of others.
You should be thanking me. I was the only one who answered to your pathetic little wish and let you forget everything you wanted to run from.

The girl's lips trembled. The searing pain exploding in her mind nearly brought her to her knees. Yet, she forced herself to stay upright, refusing to show even a hint of weakness to the being that stole her precious memories.
I won't let you mock anyone's dreams!
However, someone had already stood up before her, voicing the words she wanted to scream out but could not.
We<//Humans> have our weaknesses, yes. But the ability to feel that weakness is proof that we're truly living.
You, who steal people's dreams and rob them of all hope, have no right to mock them!
The human in black robes continued to shield her from the torrent of mud raining down. In that moment, the <phonetic=Kurumi Tokisaki>girl</phonetic> knew the time had come to make her choice.
Should she keep drowning in this lie, or take up the pain and burden of being the Spirit of Time once more?
The answer to that was clear from the very beginning.
【kuroname】... I'm sorry, but I have to go on ahead. Just leave the rest to me.
She had now tasted the <phonetic=reluctance>nightmares</phonetic> of her past, and she had accepted all of <phonetic=weakness>it</phonetic>.
And now she shall turn it all into fury. It was time for her to settle the score.
I'll show <phonetic=The  Oneiros>her</phonetic> why dreams are nothing but lies in the end.
The girl crushed the pocket watch in her palm, transforming it into two flintlock pistols, one long and one short.
Even though the pain threatened to tear her soul apart, she endured nevertheless, aiming the gun at her temple without hesitation, finger resting on the cold trigger.
Next time, we'll meet again. I promise.
Time reversed within the barrel. Her soul raced backwards through the threads of causality, hurtling toward the past.
Countless images flashed before her eyes as <phonetic=Kurumi Tokisaki>she</phonetic> plunged into a world that spiraled endlessly through the stagnant void.
At first, she tried laying everything out for the <phonetic=【kuroname】>human</phonetic> from the beginning, hoping they could find a way out of this place together.
But The Oneiros quickly realized something was amiss and threatened to kill everyone in the dream world unless Kurumi surrendered Zafkiel's powers.
Naturally, she refused. So, she raised her pistol once more and rewound time again, trying to find another forward from the very beginning.
The second time around, she concealed her presence, lurking in the shadows to uncover The Oneiros's true motives.
But the Dream City was devoured all the same. Even the <phonetic=【kuroname】>human</phonetic>, who fought until the bitter end, fell into the web of the Deep Dream.
Faced with the piles of corpses before her, she shed not a single tear. She simply raised her pistol once more, silently.
Three times, four times, five times... She pulls the trigger again and again.
She could no longer recall what came after. The Dream City is corrupting her very existence, leaving her memories fractured and dim.
With each rewind, her soul returned to its original shell, carrying memories ever more fragile. She would wake again and again before that luminous stage.
"But it's not enough... I can't fall here, not yet..."
"But it's not enough... I can't fall here, not yet..."
No matter what happened, this one thought remained in her will, imprinted there like a brand of scorching iron.
In this journey that had been stretched endlessly, so much so it seemed frozen in time, she gradually picked up certain habits that seemed meaningless.

Picking a movie she's never seen at the theater, trying once more to win that black cat plushie from the capsule machine, the one that never appeared, looking up to see the surprise fireworks show over the commercial district...
<color=#34aff8ff><size=50>she only wanted to give that Commandant who's always on edge,</size></color>
<color=#34aff8ff><size=50>a brief moment to breathe between battles.</size></color>
At first, she only wanted to give that <phonetic=【kuroname】>Commandant</phonetic> who's always on edge, a brief moment to breathe between battles.
Maybe... the owner never put it in the machine to begin with. That's why I can never get the black cat.
Then we can try another convenience store and try a different machine.
Perhaps luck just hasn't come around yet. That's why you weren't able to get it today.
Whenever she voiced such pessimistic thoughts, the human beside her would always offer gentle reassurance.
<color=#34aff8ff><size=50>had become the only anchor she had in this endless cycle</size></color>
Yet, these seemingly trivial acts had become the only anchor <phonetic=Kurumi Tokisaki>she</phonetic> had in this endless cycle before she realized.
Next time, we will succeed for sure.
She always murmurs these words, speaking to the countless other versions of herself.
If you simply want to take revenge against "that person," "we" have countless ways to leave this place.
But it won't be nearly enough if only a single one of "me" manages to leave.
If I disperse Zafkiel's power, I'll be able to sift through countless dreams and choose the outcome I want.
You mean to use our combined power to select a single outcome from endless possibilities?
Exactly. You'll help me, won't you... "me"?
A bold plan. It might not work, but I'm with you.
Since I dislike bad endings, if the future isn't what I want it to be, then I'll simply overturn it with my own hands.
Their brief exchange comes to an abrupt end.
The other Kurumi Tokisaki gently closes the pocket watch and turns away, stepping forward with her head held high toward that unchosen future.
The girl who remains raises Zafkiel slowly, aiming it at her own temple.
Alright then, I'll see you soon, "me."
